subject: Pass-through vs blended pricing for HIPAA residency + HSM cost
messages:
From: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: WellProcurement <procurement@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Breakdown request — residency + HSM pass-throughs

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looks strong. Procurement asked me to follow up on the compliance add-ons pricing we discussed: audit log retention, KMS/HSM seats, and data residency (HIPAA region). They need an itemized cost schedule we can circulate to our finance team and GRC.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you provide both a pass-through model (showing actual vendor/HSM seat costs + Redwood margin) and a blended/residency surcharge model (one-line surcharge per monthly committed unit)?
- If we choose a committed volume (12–24 month), what discounts can you offer against the HSM seat amortization or residency surcharge? Finance is particularly sensitive to one-time CAPEX-like items vs recurring charges.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the fields they want filled out (ClearPath_Itemized_Ask.xlsx). We also need SOC2 in-scope evidence and an estimate of implementation effort (hours) for on-prem proxying for HSM key wrap.

Can you get something over by EOD Thursday (2/16)? We are trying to hit the legal review window for March procurement.

Thanks,
Clara
Clara Ruiz
Director, Procurement
ClearPath Health
[Attachment: ClearPath_Itemized_Ask.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Breakdown request — residency + HSM pass-throughs (need pricing input)

Team — forwarding ClearPath ask. Key constraints: they want both pass-through transparency and a single-line option for budgeting. Two levers I think we can present:

Option A — Pass-through (transparent):
- HSM seat cost (vendor list price) + 15% Redwood implementation & management fee
- Audit retention charged per GB-month at tiered rates with retention multipliers
- Residency surcharge is per-region egress/infra pass-through

Option B — Blended Residency Surcharge (one-line):
- Monthly commitment (committed RPU/throughput) + flat residency surcharge per committed unit (this amortizes HSM + audit retention)
- Offer concession if they commit 12/24 months: 20% off the residency surcharge for 12m, 30% for 24m; HSM seat amortization can be spread and credited against first 6 months of invoices

Questions for pricing and sales ops:
1) Ben — do we have standard language/percent for the 15% management fee on pass-throughs?
2) Stephanie — legal will want to avoid listing vendor seat MSRP in the SOW. Can we present a field that says "HSM vendor costs (billed to Redwood)" and show the blended line instead?
3) Laura — FYI on discounts: what are our renewal triggers for pushing a deeper credit (e.g., if they convert to Dedicated later)?

I think delivering both is the right move; buyer can choose transparency or a tidy OPEX line. Need numbers by EOD Thurs to meet their ask.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Breakdown request — residency + HSM pass-throughs (need pricing input)

Jordan — quick math and recommended play:

Assumptions (example customer profile): 10M tokens/mo (mixed gen + embeddings), 2 HSM seats for key management, 1 TB audit logs/month, 99% in-us residency.

Vendor HSM cost: $3,500/seat/mo (market list) -> $7,000/mo total
Pass-through model: Redwood management fee 12% (we've been using 12% in >50% of deals recently)
- HSM line: $7,000 + 12% = $7,840/mo
- Audit logs: $0.02/GB-month -> ~$20/mo for 1TB*1000GB? wait — our current audit pricing uses compressed storage. Estimate $200/mo for 1TB retained 90 days -> need to confirm storage multiplier

Blended surcharge model: amortize HSM + expanded audit retention into a residency surcharge of $3.50 per committed 1k tokens equivalent for this profile.
Discount play:
- 12mo commit: 18% off surcharge (round to 20% for negotiation room)
- 24mo commit: 28% off (round to 30%)

Concession mechanics: if they push back on CAPEX visibility, we present the blended line and include an appendix with a "confidential vendor cost summary" (for legal use only). Avoid publishing vendor MSRPs in the SOW.

I can produce the two-sheet pricing table with per-line math and a sliding scale for commit tiers. Laura/Stephanie: callout any compliance/contract issues on the appendix approach.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Pricing Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Pass-through and blended options — ClearPath itemized response (attached)

Hi Clara — thanks for the clear template. Attached are two options and an implementation estimate (RWI_HIPAA_Residency_Options.pdf):

1) Transparent pass-through model (line-item):
- HSM seats (2): $7,000/mo (vendor charges) + Redwood management fee (12%) = $7,840/mo
- Audit logs: $0.20/GB-month (compressed, searchable) -> estimated $200/mo for your projected 1TB/month active volume (90-day retention)
- Residency infra surcharge: $1,200/mo (regional infra + monitoring + additional SLAs)
- Implementation: estimated 40–60 engineer hours for HSM proxying and integration (billed as fixed SOW or T&M)

2) Blended residency surcharge (one-line OPEX):
- Monthly commitment (example: 10M tokens/mo) + residency surcharge of $3.25 per 1k-token-equivalent to cover HSM amortization + audit retention.
- Commit discounts: 12-month committed term = 20% off surcharge; 24-month = 30% off surcharge.
- We are prepared to apply the first 3 months of HSM amortization as a credit on the invoice if a 24-month commit is signed within 30 days.

Confidential appendix: detailed vendor cost summary and the storage multipliers used in the audit estimate (we provide this to legal under an NDA or as an appendix in the SOW; we do not put vendor MSRP on the public SOW).

Attached: RWI_HIPAA_Residency_Options.pdf (two-page summary) and the filled ClearPath_Itemized_Ask.xlsx.

Next steps: if this aligns with finance's budgeting needs, we can draft an SOW appendix that has the blended line and the confidential appendix for legal review. Otherwise we can show the pass-through line items. Please advise which you prefer and any final questions on the implementation estimate.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0123
[Attachment: RWI_HIPAA_Residency_Options.pdf (PDF), ClearPath_Itemized_Ask.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: WellProcurement <procurement@clearpathhealth.com>, legal@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pass-through and blended options — ClearPath itemized response (attached)

Jordan — appreciate the fast turnaround and the appendix approach. A couple quick clarifications from finance and legal:
- Finance prefers the blended OPEX line for run-rate planning, but legal wants the confidential vendor appendix before we get to signature. Can Redwood attach that appendix under an NDA or include it in a closed SOW section?
- Legal asks for a 30-day ramp credit rather than 3 months amortization credit; is that flexible? They want a shorter initial credit window to avoid getting locked into long-term amortization accounting.
- Implementation hours look reasonable; can you include an estimate for a phased delivery (pilot -> full roll) and a separate line for testing/validation?

If you can update the PDF to reflect a 30-day ramp credit option and a pilot-phase implementation line (10–15 hours), we should be able to get to legal review the week of 2/27. We are leaning toward the 12-month commit + 20% surcharge discount.

Thanks — Clara
Clara Ruiz
Director, Procurement
ClearPath Health
